intro: Casargo is a mountain village at the head of Valsassina, in the Alps above Lake Como in the province of Lecco. On the slope beside the track that climbs towards Chiarino stands a lone beech with a short, enormously wide trunk and half a dozen great limbs, which a reader photographed in September and puts at around 600 years old.

trees.how_to_recognise: A lone, very broad beech on a steep grassy slope by the track, its short grey trunk crusted with lichen and gripping mossy boulders and an old dry-stone wall, half a dozen great limbs leaning out from it.
trees.access: Free. On an open mountain slope beside the track above Casargo, reached on foot. Our pin marks the area.
trees.story:
High above Casargo, on the track that climbs out of Valsassina towards Chiarino, a single beech stands out from the slope, and a reader who walked up in September sent us three photographs of it.

From below it looks like a green cloud resting on the hillside. Close to, it is something else. The trunk is short and enormously wide, grey and crusted with lichen, its base gripping mossy boulders and an old dry-stone wall, and from it half a dozen great limbs rise and lean outward before they vanish into the crown. Mountain beeches were often cut back again and again for firewood and fodder, which can leave a squat old base carrying many stems like this one, though we do not know this tree's own history.

The reader puts it at around 600 years old and its girth at 930 centimetres. Those are their figures, not a measurement we have seen, and we would love to hear from anyone who has measured it or knows what the village says about it.

Our pin marks the area on the slope. Walk round to the uphill side, where the wall meets the roots.

pin_source.note: The reader placed this pin on the map in the app; not a GPS fix.
